plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree producing fragrant five-petaled blossoms on bare branches, often before the leaves emerge. Widely cultivated in East Asia for ornament and fruit, and a key subject in traditional painting and poetry.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms herald the end of winter in East Asia and bloom before cherry blossoms; the fruit is pickled as umeboshi and used to make plum wine.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler yellow petals and slender blue-green leaves. It naturalizes in meadows, woodlands, and grassy banks and is a classic harbinger of spring in the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to April)
plants.location: Western Europe, including the UK, France, and Spain; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain toxic alkaloids, and galantamine, a compound derived from daffodil-family plants, is used in medication for Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Magnolia x soulangeana
plants.description: A large deciduous shrub or small tree with goblet-shaped flowers up to 25 cm across that open on bare branches in early spring. It is a hybrid widely planted in parks and gardens in mild temperate climates.
plants.location: Cultivated across the southeastern United States, Europe, and East Asia; originated in France
plants.funFact: This hybrid was created in the 1820s by French army officer Étienne Soulange-Bodin, and magnolias are among the most ancient flowering plant lineages, predating bees.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up leafless stalks topped with clusters of fragrant, trumpet-shaped pink flowers in late summer to autumn in the Southern Hemisphere. The strap-like leaves appear after flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn in the Southern Hemisphere (February to April)
plants.location: Native to the Western Cape of South Africa; naturalized in Australia, New Zealand, and Chile
plants.funFact: It is called 'naked lady' because the flower stalks emerge without any leaves, and it is the only species in the genus Amaryllis.
